answer: At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a hollow tag. The harbor cap is enforced at intake and juniper publishes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch however much capital it holds, because every identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 14 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
